reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it presents a Trust Wallet-styled flash-loan arbitrage bot with large crypto earning claims and directs viewers to use a linked web app. It instructs viewers to connect or unlock a wallet, select a loan amount and opportunity, and deposit and confirm a flash-loan fee or BNB payment to execute the arbitrage. Although labeled educational, the material connects the claimed earnings and estimated profit to a specific destination and wallet-confirmed payment step.

citations.quote: Trust Wallet Flash loan Arbitrage tutorial :rocket::rocket: Earn 251 ETH/BNB UniSwap and Pancakeswap 2022
Flashloans Arbitrage Bot Dapp: https://trustwallet-flashloan.web.app Open the bot with the link above, works with metamask & trustwallet browser (mobile)
Trust Wallet FlashBot will automatically check for possible arbitrage opportunity for the selected token
The bot will execute the arbitrage trades, repay back the Flash Loan amount and will split the profit between you and the developers
Check the link in the description below for the TrustWallet flashloan arbitrage bot.

opening.argument: Judge the earning headline in the context of the presentation. The opening image pairs its before-and-after balances with an explicit educational-purpose disclaimer, and the description speaks of checking for a possible opportunity, then acting only once one is found. Those qualifications matter: the material does not establish that every viewer will earn the headline amount or that an arbitrage opportunity is always available. The description also explains flash loans as a DeFi mechanism with uses beyond profit-making. Taken together, this can reasonably be read as an instructional example, not a promise of a fixed return.

citations.quote: Trust Wallet FlashBot will automatically check for possible arbitrage opportunity for the selected token
Once the opportunity has been found, you can get a Flash Loan
Flash loans are useful building blocks in DeFi as they can be used for things like arbitrage, swapping collateral and self-liquidation.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution's headline quote establishes an earnings claim, but not a guaranteed payout to each viewer. Its bot description says it checks for a possible opportunity; that conditional wording is easy to lose when the title is read alone. The linked app and payment step warrant scrutiny, but neither quote proves that the described trade cannot occur. The educational disclaimer alongside the opening balances is relevant context for how the demonstration presents itself.

citations.quote: Earn 251 ETH/BNB
Trust Wallet FlashBot will automatically check for possible arbitrage opportunity

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The disclaimer does not undo the call to use the specific linked bot. The video instructs viewers to deposit a flash-loan fee and confirm it from their wallet, while the opening image places the educational disclaimer beside a striking before-and-after balance claim. Conditional wording about finding an opportunity does not address the risk created by directing viewers to pay into this proposed profit workflow.

citations.quote: Flashloans Arbitrage Bot Dapp: https://trustwallet-flashloan.web.app Open the bot with the link above
Deposit flashloan fee into the contract. Confirm the fee from your wallet

opening.argument: This is organized as a worked tutorial. The speaker introduces a lesson on how the bot works, uses Dogecoin as an example, and tells viewers to obtain a token address through Etherscan or BSCscan before entering token details. The sampled sequence follows those operational steps through a token page, a token-entry screen and a loan-selection screen. That specificity supports reading the video as a demonstration of a proposed workflow. A tutorial can mention an app and show a fee screen without the footage itself establishing that the service is fraudulent.

citations.quote: Today, we will be talking about TrustWallet FlashLoan arbitrage bot. We will be talking about how it works and how you can use it perfectly.
In this video, I'll be using Dogecoin for an example. So paste the token address and symbol into the box

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution treats instruction as proof of solicitation. Yet its quoted description also explains a sequence of checking for opportunities, obtaining a loan and executing trades; the speaker's example walks through token selection. The linked destination shows where the demonstration takes place, not whether the depicted service actually misappropriates funds. The wallet and fee steps are important evidence, but their presence alone does not settle what happens after payment.

citations.quote: Once the opportunity has been found, you can get a Flash Loan from AAVE, PancakeSwap/UniSwap or Multiplier-Finance
In this video, I'll be using Dogecoin for an example.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The operational detail is precisely what makes the video actionable. It does not merely explain flash loans: it sends viewers to the bot link, tells them to select a purported profit opportunity, and then instructs them to deposit and confirm a fee from their wallet. The demonstrated fee screen reinforces that payment step. Calling the sequence a tutorial does not separate the lesson from its promoted, profit-seeking transaction.

citations.quote: Check the link in the description below for the TrustWallet flashloan arbitrage bot.
set the amount you want to loan and choose the best profit opportunity for the flashloan. Deposit flashloan fee into the contract. Confirm the fee from your wallet

opening.argument: The description presents a service model: the bot would find an opportunity, execute trades, repay the loan and take a stated share of any profit. A stated developer share is consistent with a paid service; it does not, by itself, establish deception. The footage shows a fee-deposit step, but these materials do not establish who receives that payment, whether a trade executes, or whether a user suffers a loss. They also do not show a request for a wallet recovery phrase. The evidence supports scrutiny of a promoted crypto service, not certainty about an unseen outcome.

citations.quote: The bot will execute the arbitrage trades, repay back the Flash Loan amount and will split the profit between you and the developers (only 0.2% of the profit will go to devs).
Deposit flashloan fee into the contract. Confirm the fee from your wallet

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution correctly identifies a linked app, an earnings pitch and a wallet-confirmed fee. Its cited material does not establish that the fee is stolen or that the described arbitrage never runs. The description explicitly says the proposed service repays the flash loan and splits profit with developers. That claim may be unverified, but an unverified service claim is not the same evidence as a demonstrated fraudulent outcome.

repay back the Flash Loan amount and will split the profit between you and the developers

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A demonstrated loss is not necessary to evaluate what this video asks viewers to do. It advertises substantial crypto earnings, directs them to a specific bot, and walks them through a wallet-confirmed fee deposit to pursue a claimed profit. The proposed developer share does not verify the bot's trades or justify paying the fee. On the available evidence, the payment instruction is part of the promoted returns mechanism, not merely background information about a service.
